items.title: mg to mcg: a simple conversion
items.description: 1 mg equals 1,000 mcg. Multiply mg by 1,000, or divide mcg by 1,000. Our free converter shows both units. Mass conversion only; it does not choose an amount to take.
items.prerequisite: Owner approved shared WEB IQ accounts; use only dedicated BACwater categories and verify publication.
items.altText: Mass conversion reference: 1 mg equals 1,000 mcg; 0.125 mg equals 125 mcg.

items.title: U-100 units and mL: know the difference
items.description: On a U-100 scale, 100 units equals 1 mL. A scale reading is not a mass in mg or a product amount in IU. Our free converter checks the arithmetic. Verify the actual device scale.
items.prerequisite: Owner approved shared WEB IQ accounts; use only dedicated BACwater categories and verify publication.
items.altText: U-100 scale reference: 100 units equals 1 mL; 25 units equals 0.25 mL.

items.title: What does mg/mL mean?
items.description: Concentration is mass divided by final solution volume. In this arithmetic example, 12 mg in a final volume of 4 mL equals 3 mg/mL. Our calculator uses your own numbers. This is not a preparation instruction.
items.prerequisite: Owner approved shared WEB IQ accounts; use only dedicated BACwater categories and verify publication.
items.altText: Concentration example: 12 mg divided by a final volume of 4 mL equals 3 mg per mL.

items.title: BACwater.ai | Same mass, different final volume
items.description: Double the final volume while keeping the same dissolved mass, and concentration halves: 12 mg in a final 4 mL = 3 mg/mL; the same 12 mg in a final 8 mL = 1.5 mg/mL. Use final solution volume, which is not always the water added. Check your own stated values with our free calculator. Laboratory research arithmetic only, not mixing instructions or dosing advice. items.title: 0.1 mL and 0.10 mL mean the same volume
items.description: A trailing zero does not change a decimal value: 0.1 mL = 0.10 mL. On a U-100 scale, 0.10 mL × 100 = 10 scale units; reverse-check: 10 ÷ 100 = 0.10 mL. Verify the actual device ratio, capacity, and printed graduation spacing. Research arithmetic only, not medical guidance. Published by WEB IQ for BACwater.ai. The site includes disclosed affiliate links.

items.title: Why 3 mg has no single mL answer
items.description: Mass does not convert to volume without concentration. Example arithmetic: 3 mg ÷ 6 mg/mL = 0.5 mL, while 3 mg ÷ 3 mg/mL = 1 mL. Same mass, different concentration, different volume. Keep units visible and use the exact stated concentration. Research arithmetic only, not medical guidance. Published by WEB IQ for BACwater.ai. The site includes disclosed affiliate links.
items.altText: BACwater.ai guide showing that 3 mg has no single mL answer without concentration. It compares 3 mg divided by 6 mg per mL, which equals 0.5 mL, with 3 mg divided by 3 mg per mL, which equals 1 mL.
